analysis.investment_thesis: On pure Magic Formula screening, GB Logistics looks attractive — a P/E of 2.64 implies an earnings yield near 38% and ROCE of 28.2% signals capital-efficient operations. However, a 29.5 Cr market cap, a 2019-incorporated issuer, and a commoditized FTL/trading model make the quality score suspect and the screen likely over-flattering.
key_strengths: Extremely high earnings yield (~38% implied from P/E of 2.64)
ROCE 28.2% and ROE 26.4% — both well above Magic Formula thresholds
Promoter holding 52.4% signals skin in the game
key_risks: Nano-cap (29.5 Cr) with ~4 years of operating history — metrics likely unsustainable
FTL freight + trading is a low-moat, commoditized business with thin structural margins
Near-zero institutional ownership (FII 0.29%, DII 2.18%) — no independent diligence
red_flags: Company incorporated 2019; single-digit P/E often signals market skepticism on earnings durability
Trading revenue can inflate turnover/ROCE without real economic value-add
analysis.detailed_analysis: The Magic Formula would rank GB Logistics highly: earnings yield implied by a 2.64 P/E is roughly 38% (even after adjusting EBIT/EV for any net debt, it almost certainly clears the 15% "very attractive" bar), and ROCE of 28.2% is comfortably above my 25% "excellent" line. On paper, this is the textbook cheap-and-good combination the formula is designed to surface.
